items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: who was on banjo for Celestan? Is that guy probably French?

ctx.x: No, that's true. He doesn't use it. What about, did you think there was any difference in the rhythm sections between colored and white?

Yeah, contrary to a lot of, to many people's opinion, we call it two beat, two four Dixieland music. It's associated with that. And the thing that surprised me the most is that these guys, for the most part, lay down a heavy four beat rhythm, you see. Just a punching style, you know, just a pounding style. And one of the few, a few musicians that I work with, I got to know very well, that had a light two beat style was Ray Badouk, Monk Hazel, you see. But for the most part, take Paul Barberin, you know, he laid…
The guy that calls himself now probably French, I can't remember. He's the leader of the band, which has called itself the Celestan Band. I'm not sure whether he was playing for them then, maybe.
